dedupe_keys.name: us epa rcrainfo biennial report data hazardous waste generated and managed by every large generator and treatment storage and disposal facility

description: The RCRAInfo Biennial Report data record how much hazardous waste each large generator in the United States produces, and how and where it is treated, stored, recycled or disposed of, facility by facility. They come from RCRAInfo, the national system the US Environmental Protection Agency keeps under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, fed by state environmental agencies from the reports handlers must file. Each row describes a waste stream at a handler identified by EPA ID, name, address and county, with the waste codes and description, tons generated and tons managed, the management method and whether it was handled on site or shipped to another facility; the RCRAInfo search adds handler identification and location, permit and closure status, compliance and cleanup information. The data are free and available through the Envirofacts REST web services as JSON, CSV or XML, through the RCRAInfo search and query builder, and as downloads. Caveats: not every hazardous waste handler files a biennial report, waste codes need the federal and state code lists, and table names in the web services must be taken from the data model. Simulation uses: building the network of hazardous waste flows from generators to treatment and disposal facilities, estimating facility capacity use, and screening facilities against flood or hurricane hazards. Related records: the GAO study of climate risk to these facilities (case_study-gao-hazardous-waste-tsdf-climate-risk) uses the same facility universe, and the Basel Convention reporting (data-basel-convention-national-reporting) covers international movements.
